items.claim: The 17:5-17:11 span is byte-warranted at its onset and disclosure-complete: a verse-initial divine koh-amar, an exact in-span ketiv/qere accounting whose splices stop clear of every doubled reading, correctly typed marks, and the blessed/scribe homograph resolved the right way.
items.evidence: Frame ownership verified in the bytes rather than asserted: 17:5 opens verse-initially with כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.17.5, byte tier), the divine mouth, with no quoted-prophet or letter-embedded owner anywhere in the window, so the koh-amar cited as the onset signal genuinely carries a frame owner. The three-note ketiv/qere count stated for the span is exact against the inventory: MT 17:8, MT 17:10 and MT 17:11 are the only notes between 17:5 and 17:11, and no splice runs through a doubled reading - the 17:10 splice stops at בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.17.10, byte tier), ahead of that verse's doubled token. Mark disclosure is complete and never conflates the types: setumah at MT 17:4 ahead of the opening, setumah at MT 17:6 and MT 17:10 inside the span, and 17:11 genuinely unmarked (tier-3, single-witness, and absence is not treated as counterevidence). The token trap at 17:7 is disarmed rather than tripped: בָּר֣וּךְ הַגֶּ֔בֶר (oshb:Jer.17.7, byte tier) is read as the passive participle and not as the scribe's name, which is the byte-correct reading here. One non-fatal precision note carried forward rather than charged: at 17:7, 17:9 and 17:10 the spliced Hebrew runs past the extent of the paired English gloss, so gloss extent and splice extent do not match.

items.claim: The two-verse doxology cut leaves a byte-true catchword bond undisclosed: the shaming verb on which 17:13 closes is picked up at 17:18, bracketing 17:14-17:18 and arguing that 17:12-13 belongs with the petition rather than standing as its own unit.
items.evidence: The span's own closing splice ends on the catchword itself - כָּל עֹזְבֶ֖יךָ יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ (oshb:Jer.17.13, byte tier) - and 17:18 opens יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ רֹדְפַי֙ וְאַל אֵבֹ֣שָׁה אָ֔נִי (oshb:Jer.17.18, byte tier), where the same verb recurs and is then negated for the speaker. The two forms are identical once cantillation is stripped (they differ only in the accent), and a skeleton sweep on the attested form returns 5 verses book-wide on MT keys, of which exactly two fall in ch 17, MT 17:13 and MT 17:18 (identity numbering here - the book's single offset zone is confined to chs 8-9, and no digit in this item touches it). That is a byte-true device straddling this span's own closing seam, and it appears nowhere in the reasoning: the rival reading weighed is only the backward one, folding into 17:5-11 on addressee grounds, so the forward bond that actually contests the cut is never faced. Two supporting observations, neither decisive on its own: the tier-3 segmentation groups 17:11-13 together, so the span's opening seam falls inside a single marked segment while only its closing seam aligns to one (single-witness, weak corroboration, absence never counterevidence); and a two-verse unit at this granularity is the over-split direction, which raises the bar the undisclosed bond does not clear. What the row gets right is recorded: the setumah at MT 17:13 is correctly typed and disclosed, and the ketiv/qere note in that same verse is correctly placed after the splice, which stops before the doubled reading.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep: 5 verses book-wide, MT keys

items.claim: The 17:14-17:18 confession is byte-bounded at both edges - a first-person petition onset carried by the pointed forms and a genuine tier-1 divine commission at 17:19 - with complete mark disclosure and no ketiv/qere owed.
items.evidence: The opening turn stands on the bytes and not on a rendering: 17:14 begins רְפָאֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Jer.17.14, byte tier) and repeats the shape in הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נִי (oshb:Jer.17.14, byte tier) - imperatives carrying a first-person singular object suffix, and both witnesses render them as the speaker's own petition, which is the standard this book's staged material allows for a form-class claim since no morphology layer is available. The closing seam is carried by an onset rather than by a mark alone: 17:19 opens verse-initially כֹּה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Jer.17.19, byte tier), a divine koh-amar with the prophet as addressee, so the unit closes where a fresh frame owner speaks. Mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed for the window (setumah at MT 17:13 ahead of the opening, setumah at MT 17:18 at the close; tier-3, single-witness), and the span carries no ketiv/qere note at all, so nothing is owed on that arm. The shaming-verb bond linking 17:13 to 17:18 is real and undisclosed, but the pressure it creates falls on the 17:12-13 unit's own boundary: this span is independently bounded by its petition onset and by the commission at 17:19, and its extent matches the confession shape the bytes support.

items.claim: The 17:19-17:27 commissioned proclamation is byte-warranted end to end: a verse-initial koh-amar-to-me commission, an exact in-span ketiv/qere accounting, and a correctly typed closing petuchah standing where the next frame's word-event header opens.
items.evidence: The onset is verified in the bytes: 17:19 opens כֹּה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הָלֹ֤ךְ וְעָֽמַדְתָּ֙ (oshb:Jer.17.19, byte tier) - divine mouth, prophet as addressee, verse-initial - so the commission claim is not a translation artifact. The three-note ketiv/qere count stated for the span is exact against the inventory (MT 17:19, MT 17:23 and MT 17:24 are the only notes between 17:19 and 17:27), and the opening splice stops before 17:19's own doubled reading, so nothing is sliced through a variant. Mark disclosure is complete and the types are never conflated: setumah at MT 17:18 ahead of the opening, setumah at MT 17:20 inside, petuchah at MT 17:27 at the close (tier-3, single-witness), and the closing mark is correctly identified as sitting at the seam where the following frame's header opens - which the bytes confirm, since 18:1 carries the prose-sermon superscription shape with alef-lamed. Keeping the relay command of 17:20 with the material it introduces is consistent with the bytes: no fresh frame owner intervenes inside the span. One interior signal worth naming and rightly not treated as a closing device: 17:24 carries the neum token mid-span (sweep: 4 verses carry that token across chs 17-19, at MT 17:24, MT 18:6, MT 19:6 and MT 19:12), which is corroboration only.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep: 4 verses carrying the neum token in chs 17-19

items.claim: The frame verification for this span holds byte for byte, but its ketiv/qere disclosure is asymmetric - one of the two in-span notes goes unmentioned in the very verse the rival reading names - and the potter-word recurrence is asserted as identity without a tier and is not token-identical.
items.evidence: What holds is substantial and is recorded first: 18:1 opens verse-initially הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.18.1, byte tier), and the linking particle is אֶֽל (oshb:Jer.18.1, byte tier) with alef-lamed, so this is the prose-sermon superscription shape and not the one-site ayin-lamed 'concerning' variant that a careless reading blends into it; the internal word-event is equally real, 18:5 reading וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.18.5, byte tier), verse-initial. All five in-span marks are disclosed with the correct type and never conflated. Two defects. First, ketiv/qere disclosure is asymmetric: the span carries two notes, at MT 18:3 and MT 18:10, and only the 18:3 note is disclosed, although MT 18:10 shows the doubled reading plainly in the bytes - וְעָשָׂ֤ה הרעה הָרַע֙ (oshb:Jer.18.10, byte tier) - and 18:10 is precisely the verse the rejected reading names, so the note is engaged without being disclosed. Second, the recurrence claim carries no tier label and overstates what collate supports: the potter tokens at 18:2, 18:3, 18:4 and 18:6 are the article-bearing form הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.18.3, byte tier) - skeleton sweep on that attested form: 5 verses book-wide, MT 18:2, MT 18:3, MT 18:4, MT 18:6 and MT 19:11 - while the form at 18:11 is the bare יוֹצֵ֤ר (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier). The shared object is the lexeme, not an identical token; calling it the identical word with no tier named is not collate truth, and the boundary argument that rests on it inherits the imprecision.

items.claim: Both stated warrants for cutting at 18:13 fail against the bytes - direct address does not stop at the claimed seam and the cited speech formula brings no change of frame owner - while the remaining ground is translation layout, a root-play brackets the span on both sides undisclosed, and an in-span ketiv/qere note is not disclosed.
items.evidence: First, the claimed turn from direct second-person address to third-person description is contradicted by the span's own opening verse: 18:13 reads לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַֽׁאֲלוּ נָא֙ (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), whose imperative שַֽׁאֲלוּ (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier) is second-person plural and is rendered as an imperative by both witnesses, so direct address continues straight across the claimed seam. Second, the speech formula cited as the substrate signal brings no frame-owner change: the same divine formula already stands inside 18:11, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier), the same mouth, and 18:13's formula is subordinated to verse-initial לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), which binds it to what precedes as consequence rather than opening a new owner - a formula onset without an owner change is not a tier-1 cut. Third, the surviving ground is the poetry-line contrast; the digit is accurate against the folded rendering, but line-break layout is translation-side metadata that is never boundary evidence in either direction, and the staged original-language material carries no verse-structure layer, so no byte fact stands behind the prose-to-poetry turn as stated. Fourth, cross-seam cohesion runs against the cut on both sides and is undisclosed: 18:11 carries וְחֹשֵׁ֥ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מַֽחֲשָׁבָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) and 18:12 closes אַחֲרֵ֤י מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.18.12, byte tier) immediately before the span, while 18:18 opens וְנַחְשְׁבָ֣ה עַֽל יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת֒ (oshb:Jer.18.18, byte tier) immediately after it - sweeps on the attested forms, MT keys: the plural noun 9 verses book-wide, of which only MT 18:12 and MT 18:18 fall in chs 17-19; the singular noun 2 verses; the suffixed plural 1 verse; the cohortative verb 1 verse. Fifth, the span carries a ketiv/qere note at MT 18:16, visible in the bytes as לְשַׁמָּ֖ה שרוקת שְׁרִיק֣וֹת (oshb:Jer.18.16, byte tier), inside the charge the reasoning itself recites, and it is not disclosed while the flanking spans disclose theirs.
tier_citations: skeleton sweeps, MT keys: 9 / 2 / 1 / 1 verses on the four attested forms

items.claim: The 18:18-18:23 confession is byte-bounded and disclosure-complete: a verse-initial narrative report of the plot, both in-span ketiv/qere notes disclosed with the closing splice standing clear of the doubled reading, and correctly typed marks.
items.evidence: The onset is verified verse-initially: 18:18 opens וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לְכ֨וּ וְנַחְשְׁבָ֣ה עַֽל יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת֒ (oshb:Jer.18.18, byte tier), and the prophet is named in the long attested spelling, so the sweep hazard by which the deceit noun sits inside that name is not tripped - the name is handled as a token, not as a substring. Both ketiv/qere notes in the span are disclosed (MT 18:22 and MT 18:23), and the closing splice בְּעֵ֥ת אַפְּךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֥ה בָהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.18.23, byte tier) takes the verse's final clause, standing clear of the doubled reading earlier in that same verse, so nothing is sliced through a variant. Mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 18:17 ahead of the opening and setumah at MT 18:23 at the close; tier-3, single-witness), and 18:23 is the only mark inside the span. The paseq at MT 18:20 is a count-only inventory object and no position claim is made about it, so nothing is owed there. The devising-root tie that binds 18:18 back to 18:11-18:12 is real and undisclosed here too, but it bears on the boundary drawn at 18:13 rather than on this span's own edges, which are carried by the narrative onset and by the first-person petition body that follows it.

items.claim: The frame owner at 19:1 checks out in the bytes, but the span's stated cohesion warrant is carried by the translation - the elders thread does not exist in the Hebrew - and no ketiv/qere is disclosed although a note rides on the gate name the reasoning itself recites.
items.evidence: Frame ownership verified first, since it was the open question: 19:1 opens verse-initially כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הָל֛וֹךְ וְקָנִ֥יתָ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) - the divine mouth, with no embedded, letter-borne or quoted-prophet owner in the window - and the addressee is the prophet alone, every command in the span carrying the second-person masculine singular shape - וְקָנִ֥יתָ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) at the buying and וְשָׁבַרְתָּ֖ (oshb:Jer.19.10, byte tier) at the breaking - both rendered second-person singular by both witnesses. Mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 18:23 ahead of the opening; petuchah at MT 19:5 and petuchah at MT 19:13; tier-3, single-witness), and the interior neum digit is right and correctly read as texture (sweep: 2 verses in ch 19 carry the token, MT 19:6 and MT 19:12). Three defects. First, the span carries a ketiv/qere note at MT 19:2 and none is disclosed anywhere in the row, although the doubled reading rides on the gate name itself - שַׁ֣עַר החרסות הַֽחַרְסִ֑ית (oshb:Jer.19.2, byte tier) - inside the errand the reasoning recites verse by verse. Second, the cohesion sentence claiming that the same addressed elders carry through from the buying to the breaking holds only in the rendering: MT 19:1 has no verb governing וּמִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וּמִזִּקְנֵ֖י הַכֹּהֲנִֽים (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier), the taking being supplied on the translation side, the elders are never addressed in the bytes, and the companions at the breaking are הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַהֹלְכִ֖ים אוֹתָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.19.10, byte tier), not elders - the elders token occurs in one verse of the span (sweep: 1 verse, MT 19:1). The jar arm of that same sentence is byte-true and is credited (sweep: 2 verses book-wide carry the jar noun, MT 19:1 and MT 19:10). Third, the span is called distinct from the potter-house visit while its own opening and interpretation verses carry that unit's lexeme: 19:1 buys a יוֹצֵ֣ר חָ֑רֶשׂ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) and 19:11 breaks כְּלִ֣י הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.19.11, byte tier) - skeleton sweep on the article-bearing form: 5 verses, MT 18:2, MT 18:3, MT 18:4, MT 18:6 and MT 19:11 - an undisclosed continuity signal running against the claimed distinctness.
tier_citations: skeleton sweeps, MT keys: 1 verse (elders), 2 verses (jar noun), 5 verses (article-bearing potter form), 2 verses in ch 19 (neum token)
